findings.reason: the 30-day ceiling is half the rule and is unmeasured, so the node's gate cannot show the ceiling fires at all.
findings.text: the expiry rule is "whichever comes first" of the plan's close and 30 days, but the done-when tests only the first branch on attributed items (29 days kept until close, removed at close) and never a 31-day-old attributed item whose plan is still open; an implementation that attributes by plan and then keeps forever while the plan is open passes every case listed

findings.reason: the scope as written omits the file the mechanism runs in, which is either an immediate blocker for the node or a duplicated rule that drifts from the original.
findings.text: s4's write paths are reckon/crew/gc.py, the new test and the fragment, but the pass that removes report trees is _run_report_trees, defined in reckon/crew/routing.py and called from gc.py:807; every rule s4 adds (keep on citation, keep on persist record, plan-close attribution, items that are files rather than folders) has to be applied inside that function, so a node honouring the declared scope either stops or writes a second copy of the rule in gc.py

findings.reason: one sentence naming where the staging root is configured (a flight setting, or the persist root itself) is the difference between an implementable check and a hardcoded project path.
findings.text: the symlink rule permits a target under "that project's persist root or the move's staging root", but §2 declares only the persist root as flight configuration and the staging root appears nowhere as a setting; a node must either hardcode /work/projects/imas_gpu/crew-reports/<project> from §6, which breaks the repo-agnostic rule the plan itself asserts, or leave the second root undefined and fail its own outside-target case
